Question: How do you decide which category to put your app under in the iOS App Store?
Answer: First and foremost, make sure you choose a category that actually reflects your app’s content. Categories are meant to help people find apps that match their interests or requirements. So, if you design an app for real-time waterpolo scores, you might not want to place it in the ‘Books & Reference’ category since your target audience probably won’t be looking there. At the same time, you may want to stay away from some of the more competitive categories. Of course ‘Social’ is a really popular genre, but putting your app there means going up against Facebook, TikTok, and Twitter for downloads. Try to find a happy medium — sometimes choosing a less popular category is better for visibility. For example, it’s much easier to rank highly in the top charts in less competitive genres. Finally, one of the most common strategies for determining category placement is looking at where your most successful competitors have placed themselves. Chances are they’ve done a lot research into their ideal customer profiles and have chosen the categories that optimize their ability to reach them. By following their lead, you can make the most out of their research without substantial time or investment on your end. Finally, while mobile ads are largely centered around the two dominant platforms (Google Play and the Apple App Store), CTV is more dispersed. Roku leads the way in terms of app inventory, but not by much. Apple TV, Google TV, Fire TV are all close behind, while Samsung, LG, and Vizio are beginning to make up ground.
